subject: accessibility gap at {{domain}} — regulators are watching
body:
Hi {{first_name}},

I ran an accessibility audit on {{domain}} and found {{total_issues}} WCAG 2.1 AA violations — the kind that are drawing increasing scrutiny from regulators and plaintiff firms who treat digital inaccessibility as low-hanging fruit.

Three most urgent on {{business_name}}:

1. {{top_issue_1}} — contact forms, intake forms, and client portals with unlabeled fields or missing ARIA roles are the #1 ADA complaint against professional services sites. If a potential client can't fill out your form, you lose the lead AND open yourself to liability.

2. {{top_issue_2}} — color-only indicators for status, deadlines, or case progress fail WCAG 1.4.1. Users with color vision deficiency can't distinguish critical information from background, and courts have ruled this constitutes discrimination.

3. {{top_issue_3}} — the DOJ's 2024 rule on web accessibility explicitly covers professional services firms. Plaintiff attorneys are filing drive-by ADA suits against sites with no accessibility statement and obvious WCAG failures — your site is exactly the profile they target.

I can send {{business_name}} a full 17-point audit (with remediation code your web team can implement immediately) — free, no commitment. If you want us to fix it: flat $1,200, 2-week turnaround.

Worth 15 minutes to walk through the findings?

— Emilio Ranucoli
Systems Engineer — accessibility & compliance audits
